[In the previous article](https://www.mql5.com/en/articles/8818), I started creating the functionality for working with tick data. In particular, I created the class of tick data object. Here, I will create the list for storing such objects. Such lists will be available for each symbol used in the program. By default, the size of tick data lists for a symbol is to cover the current day. Naturally, it will be possible to set the number of days the program will have a set of tick data for.

Why do we need custom tick data lists if MQL5 allows obtaining them at any time? They allow us to search for the necessary data, as well as compare and receive data quickly and easily. This opportunity is provided by the very concept of building lists in the library and working with them.

I will combine the lists created for each symbol applied by the program into the collection of tick data that makes it more convenient to work with tick data of any symbol and perform any analysis of tick streams of different symbols.
keyword_hits: I will calculate the start of the necessary day depending on the specified number of days the tick history should be stored for. All existing ticks are to be added to the list using [CopyTicksRange()](https://www.mql5.com/en/docs/series/copyticksrange) from that day. In the next article, I will arrange the real time update of these lists to always have the relevant tick database in the collection.
